Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent that sends the whole chat to a model provider (Anthropic Messages API or OpenAI Responses API, directly or through the JusPrin Cloud gateway) on every call. Today the host rebuilds earlier turns in a shorter form at each new turn, so provider prompt caches miss and about 70% of an Opus bill was cache writes. Kenneth (the owner) is running a measured, step-by-step programme to make the history byte-stable; the working plan is the untracked file `chat-history-cache-plan.md` in the main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (read it, and `chat-history-measurement.md` next to it, but never commit either). The integration branch is `claude/chat-history-cache` (commit `cd4162fa97`), which your worktree is cut from. A key finding (M1): no full live request body exists anywhere; the app has no request-body logging and the project-prompt recorder cut stored results at 4,000 characters. Every later step (an OpenAI baseline, live before/after cache runs, checking that consecutive requests share a byte-identical prefix) needs the bodies, not just token counts. Your piece is that logging. Constraints: no live model calls of any kind (Kenneth approves paid batches individually; this task needs none). Keep production code in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` untouched unless a tiny additive seam is unavoidable; prefer a wrapping transport in test code. Commit on your branch only, no push, no merge, never stage submodules, no attribution lines in commit messages. Temp notes stay untracked in the worktree root. Shared Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, run long builds with nohup and watch the log (a foreground Bash call that times out kills the build), and never end your turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call until it finishes. Two sibling sessions work at the same time on `AgentHost.cpp` and on `ProviderAgent.cpp` plus the codecs, so add new tests at the end of test files and avoid editing those sources.

Task:
Add request-body logging to the shell harness so that every model request the Agent posts during a harness run is written to disk exactly as posted, one file per request, with the response's usage line beside it.

Where things are:
- The transport interface is `IAgentHttpTransport` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentTransport.hpp` (`post(AgentHttpRequest, EventFn)`); the Agent posts through it. The cleanest design is a logging transport in the harness that wraps whichever real or fake transport the harness builds, writes the body bytes before forwarding, and writes the usage/stop fields from the streamed response events after.
- The shell harness is `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`; `--live-agent` is handled around line 13150. Find how the live and fake transports are built and wrap them there.
- The project-prompt recorder (`tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, `requests.json`, its README) stores scripted bodies and cut stored results at 4,000 characters. Leave its format unchanged; the new log is a separate, uncut, byte-exact record.
- The Catch2 agent tests in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` show fake transports and streamed replies (`RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream`) you can reuse as models.

Deliverables:
1. A harness flag (for example `--request-log DIR`) that, when set, writes for each request `<n>-request.json` (bytes exactly as posted, plus a small sidecar or header with provider, endpoint, chat id and timestamp) and `<n>-response.json` (the usage and stop fields, and the final assembled response text if cheap to get). Numbering is per run, in post order. Works for both wire formats.
2. A Catch2 or harness test that drives a scripted (fake) run with the flag set and proves the file bytes equal what the transport posted, and that two requests give two files.
3. A small script `tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py` that takes a log directory and, for consecutive requests of the same chat, reports the length of the common byte prefix, the first differing byte offset and the JSON path at which they diverge. This is the check phase 2 will use to find cache leaks. Give it a unit test on two tiny hand-written bodies.
4. A short section in `tests/shell/README.md` (or the harness's existing doc; find which one documents flags) on the flag and the script.

Done means: the agent suite and your new tests pass in your worktree's build; a scripted harness run with the flag produces files; nothing in `requests.json` or existing baselines changed; one or a few commits on your branch with messages that explain what and why; an untracked note `request-log-report.md` in the worktree root saying what you built, how you verified it, and anything you could not verify (there is no live run, say so).

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own

## Request bodies as posted (`--request-log`)

`requests.json` holds bodies for this suite to send, with stored results cut
to 4,000 characters. To see what the app itself posts, byte for byte, give
the shell harness `--request-log <directory>` beside `--live-agent`,
`--manual-live-agent` or `--project-prompt-requests`. The directory must be
new or empty. For the n-th request of the run it writes:

- `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it.
- `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, header names (credential values
  redacted), chat id, purpose (`reply` or `title`), request id, attempt, time
  and body length.
- `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
- `NNNN-response.json`: outcome, HTTP status, usage as the provider named its
  fields, stop reason, the assembled text and any error.

```bash
build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
    --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json /tmp/requests.json --request-log /tmp/request-log
```

The scripted run sends nothing and its responses carry no usage. Only the
project chat's Agent is logged: the printer panel builds its own from the app
configuration, and so does the host when a chat picks a model other than the
one the harness installed. `tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp` wraps any
transport and agent, so another harness mode can log the same way.

`prefix_check.py` then compares each request with the one before it of the
same chat and purpose: the common byte prefix, the first byte that differs and
the JSON path it belongs to in each body. A provider caches a prompt prefix,
so a difference inside an earlier message is a cache leak; `[append]` means the
earlier body ended an array where the later one goes on with it.

```bash
python3 tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py /tmp/request-log
python3 tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py /tmp/request-log --ignore-key cache_control --json
```

`--ignore-key cache_control` leaves out Anthropic's moving breakpoint, which
differs on every request without changing what is cached; the bodies are then
compared as Python writes them back, not as posted. `test_prefix_check.py`
checks it on hand-written bodies.

# Request-body logging (L0): report

Untracked working note, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, commit `282342b918`, on top of `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`). Not pushed or merged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. Each logged reply body equals the bytes the fake received; usage, stop reason, text, project and chat id, numbering and redaction are checked. I proved it can fail: making the logger append one byte to each body gave 4 byte-equality failures and 8 length failures; restored, it passes (150 assertions).
- **Whole agent suite**: 471 test cases, 16,575 assertions, all passed (Release build in this worktree).
- **`test_prefix_check.py`**: 9 tests pass. The "an append followed by a later change is not an append" test fails when the tail condition is removed.
- **Scripted harness run**: `--project-prompt-requests` on the `direct` conversation of `script.json` (two passes, scripted model, nothing sent over the network) with `--request-log` wrote 333 requests (1,332 files, largest body 1.4 MB). `prefix_check.py` reported all 329 pairs as `[append]` and took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without `--request-log`. `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

## What I could not verify, and things to know

- **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. Real streams (OpenAI's `response.completed` usage, Anthropic's `message_start`/`message_delta` usage) follow the documented shapes the codecs already parse, but no real stream has gone through this logger yet.
- **The live harness mode only builds an OpenAI agent** on this branch. The Anthropic journey mode (`--plan-journey`) is uncommitted in `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`; to log it, wrap its `make_openai_http_transport()` with `log.transport("anthropic", …)` and its agent with `log.agent(…)`, the same way `install_harness_agent` does.
- **Not logged**: the printer panel's Agent and any agent the host rebuilds through its chat model source (a chat that picks a model other than the one the harness installed). Both are built from the app configuration through `make_openai_http_transport()` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Covering them needs a small seam in production code (for example a test-settable transport wrapper used by `make_openai_http_transport`); I did not add one.
- **Reading the byte count on OpenAI**: the app writes JSON keys alphabetically, so a Responses body opens with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. The shared byte count of a clean append is then just the earlier `input`; read the kind and the last-difference path, not the count. This is about the JSON byte order only. The order the provider caches in is its own and was not checked here.
- **Pre-existing harness failures, unrelated to this change**: the scripted run of the `direct` conversation reports `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL` and `direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL`, with and without `--request-log`. The cause is not investigated; it means `script.json`'s expectation that the `direct-change` point carries the print-issues skill no longer holds on `claude/chat-history-cache`. Re-recording `requests.json` from this branch would hit it.
- The Catch2 fake sends a second chat-title request after the second reply. That is host behaviour with this fake (the title answer is not taken), not the logger's; the test does not pin the title count.

I added request-body logging to the shell harness, committed as `282342b918` on `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c` (not pushed or merged). With `--request-log <empty dir>`, every request the project chat's Agent posts is written to disk exactly as posted, next to a file with the response's usage, stop reason and text. It works with `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. All tests pass. No model was called.

**Files per request** (numbered in post order):
- `NNNN-request.json`: the exact posted body.
- `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers with credentials hidden, project id and chat id, whether it is a reply or a chat-title request, request id, attempt, time.
- `NNNN-response.sse`: the raw response stream.
- `NNNN-response.json`: outcome, HTTP status, usage, stop reason, assembled text, error.

The logging code is a test-only header, `tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`, that wraps any transport and agent. Production code and CMake files are unchanged.

**`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py`** compares consecutive requests of the same chat. It reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, and the JSON path of the first and last difference. It marks a pair `[append]` only when the later body is the earlier one with items added to one array and every other byte unchanged.

One thing to know when reading its output: the app writes JSON keys in alphabetical order, so a Responses body starts with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. On OpenAI the shared byte count of a clean append is therefore small; go by the append/changed result and the last-difference path. `--ignore-key cache_control` leaves out Anthropic's cache marker, which moves on every request.

**Verification:**
- **New Catch2 test:** two turns on each wire format; every logged body equals the bytes the fake provider received. I made the logger add one byte to each body and the test caught it. The full agent suite passes: 471 test cases.
- **Script tests:** 9 unit tests on hand-written bodies pass.
- **Scripted harness run:** the prompt suite's `direct` conversation logged 333 requests, with bodies up to 1.4 MB. All 329 consecutive pairs came out as clean appends, and the check took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without the flag, and `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

**Gaps and findings:**
- **No live run.** The Anthropic path has only been through the fake provider.
- **Not logged:** the printer panel's Agent, and any agent the host rebuilds when a chat picks a different model. Both are built from the app configuration; covering them would need a small change in production code, which I did not make.
- **Anthropic journey mode:** the `--plan-journey` mode in the `opus-cost-batch` worktree is uncommitted. To log its requests it needs the same two wraps that `install_harness_agent` now uses.
- **Existing failures on the integration branch:** the scripted `direct` run fails two prompt-recorder checks, `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues` and `direct-change_sent_once_0`, with or without the flag. I did not look into the cause. Re-recording `requests.json` from `claude/chat-history-cache` will hit them.

The full report is the untracked `request-log-report.md` in the worktree root, and a short hand-over note is `L0-request-log.md` in the shared notes folder.
